title: How LLMs Distort Our Written Language
abstract: arXiv:2603.18161v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are used by over a billion people globally, most often to assist with writing. In this work, we demonstrate that LLMs not only alter the voice and tone of human writing but also consistently alter the intended meaning. First, we conduct a human user study to understand how people actually interact with LLMs when using them for writing. Our findings reveal that extensive LLM use led to a nearly 70% increase in essays that remained neutral in answering the topic question. Significantly more heavy LLM users reported that the writing was less creative and not in their voice. translated_title: 大型语言模型如何扭曲我们的书面语言
translated_abstract: arXiv:2603.18161v2 公告类型：替换交叉 摘要：大型语言模型（LLMs）被全球超过十亿人使用，最常见的是用于辅助写作。在这项工作中，我们证明了LLMs不仅改变了人类写作的语音和语气，还持续改变了预期含义。首先，我们进行了一项人类用户研究，以了解人们在使用LLMs进行写作时实际如何互动。我们的发现揭示，大量使用LLMs导致近70%的论文在回答主题问题时保持中立。显著更多的重度LLM用户报告称，写作缺乏创造力且不符合他们的个人风格。接下来，利用一个在2021年LLMs广泛发布之前收集的人类写作论文数据集，我们研究了要求LLM根据数据集中的人类书面反馈修改论文，如何引起结果内容和含义的显著变化。我们发现，即使LLM被提示专家反馈，也会导致内容发生重大改变。
tldr: 这项研究通过用户研究和数据集分析，揭示大型语言模型在辅助写作时不仅改变写作风格和语气，还显著扭曲了原始意图，导致大量文本内容趋于中立和失去个性。
en_tdlr: This study reveals through user studies and dataset analysis that large language models, when assisting writing, not only alter style and tone but also significantly distort the original intent, leading to neutralized and de-personalized content.
